description: ARC-4 methods that Phase 2 (scripts/principal-phase2-upgrade-targets.ts) may remove from a deployed program without --accept-removed, because Kyle accepted each removal as a decision. Each entry names the decision (docs/principal-resolution/PHASE-0-SPEC.md section 9.4, or a review finding id that Kyle decided), its date, the Phase 2 target, the sha256 of the deployed approval program that routes the method (a key of principal-deployed-abi.json), and the exact signature. Any removal not listed here is still refused. Unit test: smart_contracts/arc58/plugins/update-akita-dao/rollout.test.ts checks that every entry exists in the deployed-ABI snapshot.

removals.note: Deployed 10-argument newAccount; replaced by the 11-argument form with automaticUpdates (ABI change decided 2026-10-03). No shim. Ship the SDK release with the 11-argument newAccount in lockstep with the AbstractedAccountFactory upgrade: older SDKs (HEAD/published WalletFactorySDK.new/newWallet) cannot create wallets on the upgraded factory, and the new SDK cannot create wallets before it; every off-chain service that creates wallets updates at the same time. Welcome and the Guild contracts call the 11-argument form: deploy them (or switch any existing instance over) in the same execution as the factory upgrade or right after it, never before. None is deployed on MainNet or TestNet.

Deployed creation selector (no minEntries, no hint). Legacy creation shims deleted: the HEAD SDK direct quote hard-codes the old child schema and is 107,000 microALGO short of the new child. Raffle creation through deployed RafflePlugins already fails on the deployed factory (audit AR-14); nothing changes for them. Direct creation with the HEAD SDK works today and stops when this upgrade executes: ship the new SDK in lockstep. Wallet users get raffle creation with the Phase 3 v3 RafflePlugin.
Deployed prize-box creation selector (no minEntries, no hint). Same decision and consequence as the newRaffle entry.

Deployed accept without the offer terms hash; replaced by accept(pay,uint64,byte[32][],byte[32])void, which binds acceptance to the offer terms (audit C-3). A shim with the old selector would reintroduce C-3. Kyle, 2026-10-05: "fix all of them" (review 2026-10-05, ROLLOUT-2). Live callers: HyperSwapPlugin 3569561068 (granted in 7 user wallets) and 3368399121. HyperSwap has never held an offer on MainNet (offer_cursor = 0), so no open offer is stranded. The Phase 2 run of this target deploys the new HyperSwapPlugin and swaps the DAO wallet grants in the same run; user wallets reinstall through getPluginUpdate once the new id is in the SDK registry.
